Reviewers like the water-like, quick-absorbing texture and how gentle it is, including on sensitized skin using tretinoin and on very reactive skin, and several apply it by hand or on a cotton pad. Takes split on the benefit: some saw calmer redness and quick-clearing spots, while others noticed only a light soothing feel and little else, with no glow and no change in pores. Nadia Vega finds Torriden DIVE-IN Toner more hydrating but this one more soothing.

Reviewers praise the thin, fast-absorbing texture and the calm, hydrated skin it leaves, with no irritation on dry, sensitive, oily and acne-prone skin alike. Takes split on strength: some call the hydration intense and glowy, while others found it just okay, thinner than expected, or too light for dry, flaky patches, and one disliked the nutty scent. Dr. Sarah Sheu counts it among their favorites from a big range of Anua products and ranks it above Anua Heartleaf 77 Soothing Toner, which they call bland but a solid first moisturizer step.

highlights.text: too light for dry, flaky patches

paras: Reviewers agree it is very gentle and non-stripping, a fit for dry, irritated, rosacea-prone or sensitive skin and for a light morning wash. They also agree it has no lather and will not remove makeup or sunscreen, so it works as a second cleanse, and some said it left a film or residue. Things Bloggers Lied About says it has easily surpassed CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser as the go-to, while Dr Dray and Sincerely Miss Ash both prefer Aveeno Calm + Restore Oat Gel Moisturizer from the same line.

highlights.text: will not remove makeup or sunscreen

paras: Reviewers like the light, cooling gel that absorbs fast and calms redness and irritation, on sensitive, rosacea-prone, combination and oily skin alike. Takes split on moisture: some found it hydrating enough, while some said very dry skin needs a hyaluronic acid serum underneath and others found it not hydrating enough overnight, in winter or under makeup. Rudi Berry prefers it to Neutrogena Hydro Boost Gel-Cream Extra-Dry in winter for irritation or dryness but keeps that gel cream for summer, while My Skincare Regime names KraveBeauty Oat So Simple Water Cream as a similar option for irritated skin.

highlights.text: needs a hyaluronic acid serum underneath

paras: Reviewers praise it as a rich barrier cream for dry, sensitive, eczema-prone or irritated skin, from post-peel and retinoid dryness to cracked hands, and several report redness calming fast. Takes split on texture: some find it thick, greasy and slow to sink in, with a white cast until rubbed in, while others find it absorbs within minutes, and a few say it is too heavy for oily skin, though acne-prone reviewers report no clogged pores. Dr. Jenny Liu points to Avène Tolerance Control Soothing Skin Recovery Cream for rosacea flares or for anyone who dislikes the thick, pasty feel of this cream, while Dr Dray finds this one much like a similar thick barrier balm but wetter and slightly greasier.

highlights.text: thick, greasy and slow to sink in

paras: Reviewers like the cooling, soothing feel and the short ingredient list of spring water and nitrogen, using it after a shower, over makeup, before hyaluronic acid serums or to cool down in heat. Takes split on how much it does: loved-it reviewers use it for redness, itching and makeup, while one reviewer adds moisturizer right after because it cannot keep dry skin hydrated, and another rates its effect on irritated facial skin as mild to moderate and finds the nozzle hit or miss.

Reviewers like it as a gentle, low-effort cleanser for dry, normal, irritated or post-procedure skin, used in the morning, as the first step of a double cleanse or when washing the face feels like too much. Takes split on cleaning power: one reviewer says it cleanses without stripping and leaves skin soft, while another admits not loving lotion cleansers because the face feels not cleaned at all and prefers a foam. One reviewer adds that rinsing it off is better day to day than wiping alone.

Reviewers like the silky, fast-absorbing gel and its easy layering, with little irritation and a subtle glow. Takes split on results: some saw redness calm and newer or post-acne marks fade slowly, while others saw no change in stubborn, older or sun-damaged dark spots, and one found it did not deeply moisturize. Keyshana Dupuy found a rival 4% niacinamide serum worked faster and repurchased only that one, while All That She Is finds The Ordinary Niacinamide 10% + Zinc 1% worked faster than this serum, which gives extra glow and hydration.

highlights.text: stubborn, older or sun-damaged dark spots

paras: Reviewers like the watery, easy-to-rinse gel and its gentleness, with a short contact time and a glow after use, including on sensitive or atopic skin. Takes split on strength: one reviewer saw texture improve with every use, while another found it just okay, not mind-blowing, and disliked the pump, which gives tiny squirts, and a chemical smell. One reviewer adds that it can leave skin a little dry, so very dry skin may not suit it.

Reviewers praise a light, gentle gel that rinses clean and takes off sunscreen and most makeup without drying skin out. Takes split on who it suits: one reviewer recommends it for sensitive skin and thinks it fits acne-prone skin most, while another says dry, sensitive or acne-prone skin should avoid it because of the geranium maculatum oil. It adds no hydration, so a moisturizer is still needed. DEWILDESALHAB prefers a foam cleanser from the same line, which leaves them feeling less oily for the rest of the day.

highlights.text: takes off sunscreen and most makeup

paras: Reviewers praise a light gel that sinks in quickly, hydrates well and feels cooling from the metal applicator, with several noting less puffiness. Takes split on the applicator and on moisture: one says it warms up and does not always roll smoothly, another finds the roller sharp in one direction, and one calls it not very moisturizing for very dry under eyes. Banya Biswas uses it in the morning only, since the copper tripeptide does not mix well with their retinol and acid nights, and prefers Beauty of Joseon Revive Eye Serum: Ginseng + Retinal at night.

Reviewers who like it describe a hydrating, fragrance-free cream that melts in, leaves skin plump and works as a night cream or a base under sunscreen. Takes split on finish and skin type: one finds it stays sticky and pills under sunscreen or makeup, another wears it under a hydrating sunscreen without it feeling heavy, and oily skin may find it too heavy. Some broke out, and some suspect coconut oil. Simone S layers Beauty of Joseon Red Bean Water Gel over it and says the gel became their favorite of the two, and An Indian Potpourri also prefers the gel for absorbing fully with no sticky residue.

Reviewers like the very light oil texture, which turns milky or emulsifies, rinses without residue and takes off sunscreen and most makeup. Takes split on the smell, which different reviewers describe as strongly herbal, like cooking oil, like peanuts or a strong ginseng scent, and one says it is why they will not buy it again. Opinions also split on skin type: one finds it great for dry and sensitive skin but not friendly for acne-prone skin, while another saw little bumps and stopped using it. My Skincare Regime finds the texture similar to SKIN1004 Centella Light Cleansing Oil, though they describe that one as scented.

Reviewers praise a very light, water-like ginseng toner that sinks in fast, soothes sensitive and reactive skin and works as a toner, essence or both. Takes split on hydration: some call it very hydrating, even for oily and combination skin, while others find it only moderately hydrating, and one with oily combination skin found it left skin dry and tight. Archee Gupta finds it slightly thicker and smoother than Beauty of Joseon Green Plum Refreshing Toner: AHA + BHA and rates it above Beauty of Joseon Glow Replenishing Rice Milk, which they found not hydrating enough in extreme winter.

Reviewers praise a watery, scent-free serum that absorbs quickly, leaves a slight glow and is gentle on most skin. Takes split on results: some saw dark spots, acne scars or uneven tone fade over weeks, while others saw little or no change in brightness after months, and one very sensitive reviewer developed reddish spots and stopped after three uses. For hyperpigmentation on the cheeks, alex greyson finds the feel almost identical to Beauty of Joseon Glow Serum: Propolis + Niacinamide and the fading faster, though the other serum did more for texture and acne. Nayatilly finds it far less effective than a ginseng and snail mucin serum from the same line, and says The INKEY List Hyaluronic Acid Serum adds moisture much better.

highlights.text: absorbs quickly, leaves a slight glow
little or no change in brightness

paras: Reviewers describe a very watery toner that sinks in quickly, adds light hydration and a soft glow, and is usually patted on by hand. Takes split on who it suits: oily and combination skin tends to like it, one says it is best suited to dry skin, and others say dry or mature skin needs more layers or a cream. A Woman's Confidence is less excited by it than by richer, more luscious milky toners, and JQ LEEJQ, who has very dry skin, says a richer cream toner they tried since has raised their expectations. No BS Beauty scores it seven against nine for a rice toner from another brand, preferring that toner's less tacky finish.

highlights.text: sinks in quickly, adds light hydration
needs more layers or a cream

paras: Reviewers like a light serum that is slightly tacky at first, then absorbs fast, adds a dewy glow, calms redness and pimples and layers well under moisturizer and sunscreen. Takes split by skin type: very oily skin may find it too dewy or shiny under makeup, and very dry skin may want more hydration, while sensitive and acne-prone skin did well on it. Comparing textures, jessmeandering finds it similar to COSRX Advanced Snail 96 Mucin Power Essence, while Kelly Driscoll calls it the acne serum of three from the same line and prefers a calming green tea serum from that line for sensitive, dehydrated skin.

highlights.text: too dewy or shiny under makeup

paras: Reviewers like a mild gel that turns into a soft foam, rinses clean and leaves skin comfortable, with a very light fruity or fresh scent. Takes split on dryness: some found it stripping, leaving skin squeaky clean or drying in winter, while others found it soft and not tight, with no irritation on sensitive or breakout-prone skin. It removes sunscreen and light makeup easily, but heavy or waterproof makeup, mascara and eyeliner need a separate remover or a second cleanse. Doctor Anne uses it as a second cleanse after Beauty of Joseon Radiance Cleansing Balm, while Miss LJ Beauty says the cleansers they usually go back to last longer than this one.

highlights.text: rinses clean and leaves skin comfortable

paras: Reviewers who like it describe a very watery toner with gentle AHA and BHA that they say helps with texture and pores on sensitive or reactive skin without sensitivity. Both advise easing in, no more than three nights a week for one and about every other night for the other, and one notes it adds no hydration. Dr. Vanita Rattan would not recommend it to skin of colour, since the glycolic acid used morning and night risks irritation, though they like pairing an AHA with a BHA. Archee Gupta finds Beauty of Joseon Ginseng Essence Water slightly thicker and better for irritated skin, and calls Beauty of Joseon Glow Replenishing Rice Milk a miss.

Reviewers mostly praise this rice and honey wash-off mask for leaving skin soft, bright and calm without the tightness of many clay masks, with several saying redness settled after the first use. Takes split on skin type and smell: some call it right for dry skin, others say it suits oily or acne-prone skin better, and the rice scent is called unpleasant by several. Manisha Mishra alternates it with Beauty of Joseon Red Bean Refreshing Pore Mask, which they pick for oilier skin, and Kelly Driscoll prefers it to Beauty of Joseon Glow Replenishing Rice Milk, whose clay left their skin tight. alex greyson found it the least drying kaolin mask they have tried but dislikes physical exfoliators and is unsure about buying it again.

Reviewers like this stick for midday reapplication: it glides on, dries matte or satin and feels light, with no white cast and no clogged pores reported. Takes split on whether it can do more than top up: one reviewer was mixed because the stick format needs many swipes, misses spots and is not water or sweat proof, and another also needs at least four passes per area. Sarah Rose ranks it third of nine sticks, finding one rival stick more weightless and another more hydrating. One reviewer warns it may be too drying for dry skin.

highlights.text: no white cast and no clogged pores

paras: Reviewers like this red bean clay mask for staying comfortable, not drying or hardening, and for slightly smoother pores, even on dry skin. Takes split on strength: one reviewer calls it a decent mild exfoliant for oilier skin but notes a strong scent and scratchy seeds, and two say it does not clear blackheads. Manisha Mishra calls Beauty of Joseon Ground Rice and Honey Glow Mask the better pick for dull, dry or sensitive skin, since it hydrates more, and suggests alternating the two.

Reviewers like this gel for its cooling, fast-absorbing, non-sticky feel, with no breakouts or clogged pores reported and a fragrance-free formula. Most pick it for oily, combination or acne-prone skin, while those with dry skin add a richer cream on top or layer it over a serum, and results are described as moisture and feel rather than dramatic change. Michelle Bali points dry skin to Beauty of Joseon Dynasty Cream instead, while An Indian Potpourri prefers this gel to that cream, finding the cream a little sticky at first and linking it to their acne. Kelly Driscoll picks it over a thinner oat gel cream whose hydration did not last on their skin.

highlights.text: add a richer cream on top

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the weightless, water-like feel and the lack of white cast, saying it sits well under makeup and suits oily or combination skin better than dry skin. Not everyone agrees: one reviewer got stinging and an itchy body rash they suspect comes from a salicylate booster, and another found it tacky, heavy and shiny in humid weather. Who What Wear and Kelly Driscoll compare it with Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun: Rice + Probiotics SPF 50+, finding this one lighter and the original creamier, with the original better for dry skin or winter. clarity kat found it the lightest of four sunscreens they tried but named Haruharu Wonder Black Rice Moisture Airyfit Daily Sunscreen the overall winner.

highlights.text: stinging and an itchy body rash
tacky, heavy and shiny in humid weather

paras: Reviewers praise the light, cream-like texture that melts in without pilling, with a soft glow, no real white cast and little scent, and several say it works under makeup. Takes split on the eyes and on shine: some report no stinging even on delicate eyes, while others get stinging if it reaches them, and very oily skin may find it too glowy. Protection is debated: one reviewer saw a slight tan after about an hour in harsh sun, and another found foundation over it reduced the layer on a UV camera. Paulina Esquivel prefers it to Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun Aqua-Fresh: Rice + B5 SPF 50+, which controls shine a little better but looks less luminous and can pill.

Reviewers like this light, quick-absorbing retinal serum for being gentle around sensitive eyes while slowly softening fine lines and brightening the under-eye area. Takes split on results and feel: most call it a gradual, gentle option, one noted it does not fix dark circles caused by poor sleep, and another found the texture slightly oily and heavier. Reviewers also advise night use, sunscreen by day, starting a couple of times a week and keeping it off the eyelid margin.

highlights.text: dark circles caused by poor sleep

paras: Reviewers praise how gently this micellar water cleans, with no perfume, no stinging around the eyes and no oily film, including on sensitive, rosacea-prone and dry skin. Takes split on makeup removal: one reviewer clears eye makeup in a single swipe and another lifts waterproof makeup with gentle pats, while another says waterproof mascara is the one thing it will not lift and heavy makeup takes several passes. The mixed reviewer got burning and redness after applying it with a baby wipe, which they blame on ignoring the label's cotton pad directions.

Reviewers praise the thin, silky milky texture that absorbs fast, leaves a glow without residue and stays gentle on sensitive and reddened skin. Takes split on weight and need: some call it light enough for oily skin and hydrating enough for dry skin, while others find it hydrating but barely moisturizing and not a must-have. Dr Dray prefers a creamier toner with macadamia seed oil after a couple of weeks and would not repurchase this one, and Made-up Mesearch ranks it a close second to Haruharu Wonder Black Rice Hyaluronic Toner.

highlights.text: thin, silky milky texture that absorbs fast

paras: Reviewers like this creamy 4% benzoyl peroxide wash for being easy to tolerate, with ceramides, hyaluronic acid and niacinamide in the base, and for cleaning without much dryness, though several note it foams little. Takes split on results: some saw blemishes clear or mask-related breakouts drop, while one found it did not help moderate hormonal acne and one very oily reviewer disliked the film it leaves. Dr Dray finds it more moisturizing and easier to tolerate on the face than another brand's 4% benzoyl peroxide creamy wash, though too slippery to work as a shower body mask.

highlights.text: did not help moderate hormonal acne

paras: Reviewers praise it as a two-in-one SPF 30 moisturizer that does not feel oily and, for several of them, caused no breakouts on acne-prone or sensitive skin. Takes split on texture: some saw no white cast at all, while others saw a white tint or coating at first that took time and rubbing to blend. Niella Obijiaku found it thicker and whiter than CeraVe PM Facial Moisturizing Lotion, which they rate as the lighter, clearer option. Allura Beauty saw it pill when layered over another moisturizer and chose a drugstore SPF 30 lotion with near-identical ingredients instead.

highlights.text: a white tint or coating at first
pill when layered over another moisturizer

paras: Reviewers mostly praise how light and quick to absorb it is, using it on the body and face with no sticky feel, and often pick it for normal, combination, oily or sweaty skin. Takes split on dryness: Mis Fashionerias On-line found CeraVe Moisturizing Cream thicker and better for dry to extra dry skin, while Olivia UKBeautyRoom, whose skin is extremely dry, finds the lotion a bit more moisturizing than CeraVe Moisturizing Cream and suggests the cream for winter. Cotton Candy Fro found it not moisturizing enough for drier patches and broke out after one use on a combination oily face, and No BS Beauty warns acne-prone skin off the face.

highlights.text: not moisturizing enough for drier patches
warns acne-prone skin off the face

paras: Reviewers mostly like it as a gentle, lightweight eye cream that hydrates and sits smoothly under concealer, with no stinging even on sensitive eyes. Results are where takes split: some saw slightly calmer puffiness and dark circles, while others saw no help for dark circles. Matt Randon compared the ingredient list with CeraVe PM Facial Moisturizing Lotion and found the same key ingredients, with the eye cream only slightly thicker, so two layers of the lotion would do the same job. Olivia UKBeautyRoom found it a bit thinner than they prefer and would pick a much richer eye cream.

Reviewers mostly praise it as a gentle, fragrance-free cleanser that foams and lifts oil, dirt and makeup without leaving skin dry or tight, especially on oily, combination and acne-prone skin. Takes split on dryness: one reviewer was left with tight, not-soft skin, while others felt no tightness at all and some saw fewer pimples. Dr. Daniel Sugai picks it over CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser for acne-prone skin because it has niacinamide, and Oluchi Onuigbo points normal to dry skin to CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser instead. Dr. Arsalan Aspires suggests sensitive skin wanting fewer actives may lean toward a simpler foaming cleanser with a self-foaming pump.

highlights.text: without leaving skin dry or tight

paras: Reviewers praise it as a night-time slugging step that seals in moisture and calms dry, flaky or retinol-irritated skin, with the ceramides and hyaluronic acid as the reason it feels better than plain petroleum jelly. Dr Dray found it plumper and better on fine lines around the eyes and on lips than a competing petrolatum ointment that contains lanolin, though that one stays the pick for first aid, while All That Glows calls it a step above plain petroleum jelly and James Welsh slightly prefers it to plain petroleum jelly. Takes split on feel and skin type: it can stay greasy and sticky for hours, may leave product on the pillow, and some reviewers hold back from recommending it for acne-prone skin, though one with acne-prone skin says it never broke them out.

highlights.text: a step above plain petroleum jelly

paras: Reviewers who loved it describe a creamy cleanser that foams a little, rinses clean and removes makeup and sunscreen without leaving skin tight or dry, including on dry, sensitive and acne-prone skin. Takes split on makeup removal and irritation: some needed two or three washes or an oil first for mascara and waxy products, and one reviewer got pimples and a chin reaction within days. Lavinia Rusanda calls it the best of both worlds between CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser and CeraVe Foaming Facial Cleanser, while Oluchi Onuigbo finds it less drying than the foaming one and liked it more than the hydrating one, which did not work for them. Twenty4kay prefers it to CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser for more moisture and better makeup removal.

Reviewers mostly like it as a soft, non-stripping cleanser with no scent and little or no lather, best for normal to dry, sensitive or winter-flaky skin. Takes split on oily skin and makeup: some found a film left behind and said it does not lift mascara, sebum or full makeup in one wash. DSBOSSKO found slightly more hydration and barrier repair than Cetaphil Gentle Skin Cleanser but picked no clear winner, and Saloni Alok Jain found their skin felt softer than with Cetaphil Gentle Skin Cleanser. Oluchi Onuigbo and Matt Randon both reach for CeraVe Foaming Facial Cleanser when skin runs oilier.

Reviewers praise it as a rich, thick seal for dry, flaky or eczema-prone skin that works on face, hands and body without fragrance. Takes split on weight and finish: some found it absorbs quickly and sits well under makeup, others found it slow to sink in, sticky or pilling, and several say it is too heavy for oily or acne-prone faces. Chitranshi preferred CeraVe Daily Moisturizing Lotion for its faster absorption, while Jime Mitzunaga preferred this cream to CeraVe Daily Moisturizing Lotion because it uses less product and absorbs faster.

highlights.text: too heavy for oily or acne-prone faces

paras: Reviewers mostly like it as a very light, quick-absorbing lotion with no residue that works at night, under makeup or in the morning with a separate sunscreen. Takes split on skin type: some found it hydrating all night on combination or dry skin, while others found it not moisturizing enough for cheeks, neck or dry areas, and sensitive skin reported tingling or burning. Beautiful With Brains is not a huge fan of CeraVe AM Facial Moisturizing Lotion with Sunscreen, which they find lightweight but not very hydrating, while Pure Glam Guide prefers this PM version over that one, which can feel thicker and leave a white cast. Zuko Nyaawie picks it over CeraVe Daily Moisturizing Lotion for its silky texture, and skyforce95 Reviews found CeraVe Moisturizing Cream too heavy and suffocating next to this lotion.

Reviewers mostly like it as an everyday gel cleanser that lathers well, cleans without a scrubby feel and adds gentle salicylic acid exfoliation for blackheads, bumps and breakouts on oily, combination or acne-prone skin. Takes split on sensitivity: several found it fine even on dry, sensitive skin, while others felt tingling, a sting around the nose or eyes, or irritation the next day, and some saw no improvement. Dr. Janet calls it CeraVe Foaming Facial Cleanser with extra exfoliating ingredients and swaps between the two, while Soso Models found it gentler than CeraVe Acne Foaming Cream Cleanser, which dried their skin out.

Reviewers praise a lightweight, gel-like serum that absorbs quickly and is gentle enough for a first retinol, with dark spots and post-acne marks fading for some reviewers over about a month. One reviewer who used it nightly for eight weeks saw no change in dark spots and noticed forehead zits, and another found two weeks too short to judge retinol results. Dr. Arsalan Aspires sets this blue bottle against a richer, creamier retinol serum in a purple bottle from the same brand, which suits dry and mature skin better, and calls this one the pick for post-acne marks and textured skin.

highlights.text: gentle enough for a first retinol
saw no change in dark spots

paras: Reviewers praise a very thick cream that leaves skin soft and plump by morning, with little to no scent and a velvety finish. Takes split on oily and acne-prone skin: one reviewer with oily skin used it nightly and loved it, while another found their face started to freak out after a few nights, especially around the nose, and kept it for the neck and dry patches. Others note that very oily skin should build up slowly or skip it.

highlights.text: freak out after a few nights

paras: Reviewers mostly praise a thin, hydrating serum that absorbs fast and layers well under sunscreen and makeup, with 10% L-ascorbic acid that feels easier on skin than stronger versions and caused little or no stinging for most. Takes split on staying power: several reviewers found the serum oxidizes quickly, turning orange or brown, and a few had tubes that leaked, cracked or came with loose caps. Sensitive skin is the other split, as one reviewer with acne-prone skin broke out repeatedly and another flagged the denatured alcohol as possibly drying, while others with sensitive or dry skin saw no irritation.

highlights.text: absorbs fast and layers well under sunscreen
oxidizes quickly, turning orange or brown

paras: Reviewers praise a silky, lightweight lotion that absorbs fast, leaves no white cast and sits well under makeup, with oily, combination and sensitive skin the best fits. Takes split on moisture and finish: one reviewer found it too matte and not moisturizing enough for dry, dehydrated skin, while others call the finish natural or glowy rather than truly matte. Dr. Daniel Sugai prefers it to the thicker CeraVe AM Facial Moisturizing Lotion with Sunscreen in summer, noting the AM lotion adds niacinamide for acne-prone skin, and benenon says the AM lotion pilled and balled up on their bare skin.

highlights.text: absorbs fast, leaves no white cast
not moisturizing enough for dry, dehydrated skin

paras: Reviewers praise a soapless, low-foam lotion that cleans without tightness and is gentle enough for sensitive, dry or reactive skin, and even works without water. The split is oily and acne-prone skin: one reviewer found it did not cleanse as much on oily skin in humid heat, and another would not recommend it for acne-prone or oily skin. Dr.Chiyen compares it with Cetaphil Daily Facial Cleanser and other versions, calling this one the choice with the fewest ingredients and lowest irritation risk.

highlights.text: not cleanse as much on oily skin

paras: Reviewers like a light gel-cream that absorbs quickly, feels comfortable around the eyes and layers under concealer without sliding. They saw little change in eye bags, dark circles or fine lines, and those with drier eyes wanted something richer. Dr. Aleksandra Brown DO, FAAD picks it for daytime and makeup, and CeraVe Eye Repair Cream for night on very dry, crepey under-eyes, while No BS Beauty prefers COSRX Advanced Snail Peptide Eye Cream for day because sunscreen does not set well over this one.

Reviewers praise a thick, rich cream that absorbs well without a greasy residue and leaves skin hydrated, with sensitive and acne-prone skin reporting no irritation or new breakouts. One reviewer loves it in winter but says it may not be best for oily skin in summer, and another saw eczema and allergy patches keep coming back, although it soothed the itching. The Pink Velvet Blog finds it thicker and more intense than a slightly runnier daily hydrating lotion from the same brand, and says it works on the face as well as the body.

highlights.text: absorbs well without a greasy residue

paras: Reviewers who liked the patches used them overnight on whiteheads and pimples that already had a head, and saw smaller, less red spots by morning, with several noting they stop picking. Takes split on closed and cystic spots and on looks: some reviewers saw no change on deep or hidden pimples, a few found the patches visible in daylight or peeling with sweat, and others call them nearly invisible. Brianna Jane prefers Mario Badescu Drying Lotion for speed, saying it worked better for them, though the patches stayed on all night where a lotion does not.

highlights.text: smaller, less red spots by morning
no change on deep or hidden pimples

paras: Reviewers praise a lightweight-feeling gel-cream that hydrates, soothes irritated or over-exfoliated skin and leaves a dewy, glassy glow, mostly on oily, combination or sensitive skin. Takes split on dryness and breakouts: one reviewer with very dry, eczema-prone skin found it stinging and drying, others with dry skin layer a thicker cream on top, and a few with oily or acne-prone skin saw breakouts. The texture is the other split, with reviewers calling it slimy, stringy or tacky and slow to sink in. Kelly Driscoll calls it a thicker gel cream with the same hydrating feel as COSRX Advanced Snail 96 Mucin Power Essence, while JQ LEEJQ likens the jelly texture to Beauty of Joseon Dynasty Cream, which they love.

highlights.text: layer a thicker cream on top

paras: Reviewers praise the hydration most: skin looks plump, soft and glassy straight after applying, and it absorbs quickly with no reaction on sensitive, combination or acne-prone skin. Takes split on what else it does: some saw calmer post-pimple redness or a softer barrier, others saw no change in acne marks or texture, and some say it supports hydration rather than transforming skin. The sticky, slimy feel can be more noticeable on oily skin, and Dr Dray cannot say whether it differs from a plain hyaluronic acid serum, since the formula already contains sodium hyaluronate, and notes the humectants need a moisturizer on top.

highlights.text: no change in acne marks or texture

paras: Reviewers mostly praise a lightweight, fast-absorbing cream that hydrates the eye area without stinging and sits well under makeup, which they say suits sensitive or easily irritated eyes. Takes split on results: some saw slightly less puffiness or a mild lift, while others saw no change in dark circles or fine lines, and peptide effects are said to need months. Dr. Ashwini Megur found COSRX Advanced Snail 96 Mucin Power Essence gave the same results and was the better pick for them, while Kelly Driscoll reads this cream as a step up from COSRX Advanced Snail 92 All in One Cream for the eye area.

Reviewers who loved it use it once a week or a few nights a week for smoother texture and small bumps on the chin and forehead, and Becca M sets it beside Sunday Riley Good Genes Lactic Acid Treatment, calling this one the plainer option with more product. Takes split on whiteheads: some saw small bumps clear, while others saw no change after weeks or months. Irritation splits too, from no stinging for some to redness and burning when used too often or in large amounts, so reviewers kept use to a few times a week at most.

highlights.text: saw no change after weeks or months
redness and burning when used too often

paras: Reviewers who loved it praise a gentle, watery toner used several times a week or nightly, with smaller-looking pores, fewer visible blackheads and no stinging, and many like the fine mist. Takes split on strength: one reviewer found it too mild to change sebaceous filaments or closed comedones, while others saw slightly clearer skin and cleaner pores. Matt Randon still prefers COSRX BHA Blackhead Power Liquid for its thicker essence feel and its help with redness, while liking this toner as AHA and BHA in one. One reviewer found it hot and irritating from the first use and pointed to a low pH.

Reviewers who loved it describe a creamy, aloe-based sunscreen that blends without white cast and hydrates enough to skip moisturizer on dry or combination skin. Takes split on skin type: oily and humid-weather users found it heavy or greasy, while others with combination oily or acne-prone skin got a skin-like finish. Pilling is the sticking point for some, as are the fragrance and alcohol in the formula, and one reviewer doubted the SPF 50+ claim until independent results are published.

Reviewers praise a rich, deeply hydrating cream that calms dry, irritated skin and retinol dryness, and they like the opaque tube as more hygienic than a jar. Takes split on daytime wear: Musings of a Muse finds it lighter and easier to wear by day than a heavier ceramide cream from another brand, while others find it too thick and hard to layer under sunscreen and makeup. Oily or acne-prone skin may find it too thick, and the bergamot oil scent bothers some even as others barely notice it.

Reviewers who liked it describe a watery, moisturizing BHA with no strong smell that does not dry the skin, used once to a few times a week, and they see it as a fit for beginners to exfoliation. Results are the split: some saw fewer blackheads and less oil within a week to a month, while others saw little change because it contains betaine salicylate rather than salicylic acid itself. Tamuno Abbey compared it side by side with Paula's Choice SKIN PERFECTING 2% BHA Liquid Exfoliant and prefers that one, which shrank pimples overnight, while this one showed nothing after half a bottle.

Reviewers who loved it praise instant, soothing hydration and a soft glow that layers well, mostly on dry, dehydrated, sensitive or acne-prone skin, with no stinging even on reactive skin. Opinion splits on oily skin and texture: one reviewer found it sticky and oily on very oily skin, and others call it slightly viscous or a little sticky when built up in layers. Banya Biswas ranks it above COSRX Advanced Snail 96 Mucin Power Essence among the COSRX toners and essences tried, and AliceintheRabbitHole ranks it first ahead of COSRX Full Fit Propolis Honey Overnight Mask.

highlights.text: sticky and oily on very oily skin

paras: Reviewers who loved it praise a gel that lathers lightly and cleans without stripping or tightness on oily, combination and sensitive skin, with the tea tree scent liked by some and called strong by others. The split is hydration and makeup: some say it is not hydrating, can dry skin in dry climates, and will not remove waterproof mascara or eye makeup. One reviewer broke out painfully on three tries, and a couple of reviewers said it stung their eyes.

Reviewers loved it as a gentle BHA step that leaves pores looking smaller and cleaner, with no stinging, dryness or irritation, and one pad covers the whole face. Takes differ on scent: one reviewer finds a strong medicinal smell, probably from tea tree and orange peel oil, while another notes a subtle citrus scent. The Happy Sloths compares it with COSRX AHA/BHA Clarifying Treatment Toner, finding that toner's very similar formula much gentler than salicylic acid but meant for glow in all skin types, while this pad adds tea tree oil and suits acne-prone skin.

Reviewers praise a creamy cleanser that makes a rich foam from a small amount and cleans oily, acne-prone skin without irritation, with less oil and fewer or smaller blemishes after a few weeks. The split is feel: one reviewer found it thick and greasy with an astringent finish and a lemony smell, while others found it soft, smooth and moisturizing. Jello Beans uses COSRX Low pH Good Morning Gel Cleanser in the morning and this one at night as the second step of a two-step cleanse.

Reviewers praise it as a thin, quick-absorbing first step that suits oily, sensitive and combination skin and layers under almost anything. Takes split on results: some saw clearer hydration and calmer skin, while others noticed no change in texture or redness, or in fine lines, and called it closer to a toner than a serum. Kelly Driscoll found fewer results than expected next to The Ordinary Multi-Peptide + HA Serum and rated it a booster, not a main anti-aging serum.

highlights.text: no change in texture or redness

paras: Reviewers praise it as a fragrance-free, ceramide-rich cream that hydrates without greasiness, works under makeup and sunscreen, and suits dry, sensitive, mature and combination skin. Takes differ on weight: some found it silky and quick to absorb, while others found it slow to settle, too light for dry skin in cold weather, or heavy by day on oily skin. The Strategist found the texture like CeraVe Moisturizing Cream but thicker, and kept it as the everyday option beside a richer, more expensive favorite.

highlights.text: heavy by day on oily skin

paras: Reviewers recommend it as an entry-level retinol cream, praising a light texture that sinks in without greasiness and little or no irritation, even over eczema flare-ups in one case. Takes split on results and value: some saw firmer, plumper skin and fading dark spots, while others saw no dramatic change and found the small tube poor value. alex greyson found it no different in feel from a cheaper gentle retinol cream and called it overpriced for the amount.

Reviewers who used it praise a silky, non-greasy oil that caused no irritation, even on sensitive areas and for people used to stronger retinoids. Views split on who it fits: one reviewer calls it well suited to dry skin new to retinol but warns the soybean oil can clog pores on oily skin, while another used it almost nightly on oily skin without trouble. Sheri Approved calls COSRX The Retinol 0.1 Cream the gentler choice for beginners, and Dr. Ashwini Megur finds the formula pretty much the same as another 0.5% retinol serum, with vitamin E and soybean oil added.

highlights.text: can clog pores on oily skin

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it as a gentle, hydrating night step with no scent, no irritation and a plump, soft feel by morning, and several wear it as a daytime moisturizer under sunscreen. Takes split on weight and results: dry, sensitive and combination skin did well, but it felt heavy on oily skin, brightening was slight or absent, and breakout-prone skin was told to be cautious about some ingredients. Wakisha Wazome found it sticky, slow to absorb and less nourishing than the honey version from the same line.

Reviewers praise a very light, nearly invisible lotion-gel with no white cast and no scent that sits well under makeup, and several call it a good fit for oily and combination skin in warm weather. Takes split on comfort: most had no stinging or breakouts, but one reviewer found it stings the eyes and makes base makeup peel without a gripping primer. Dry skin was told to add moisture underneath, and several noted it is not water or sweat resistant, so it fits daily use better than outdoor workouts or swimming. alex greyson finds it even lighter than COSRX Aloe Soothing Sun Cream SPF 50, which they also like.

highlights.text: no white cast and no scent

paras: Reviewers who loved it call it a strong, effective retinol cream that smoothed texture, brightened skin and faded pigmentation or acne marks, with a lightweight cream that sinks in quickly. Most warn that the 1% strength needs a slow start of once or twice a week, often buffered with a serum or moisturizer, because peeling, dryness and redness are common. Irritation split reviewers most: one with oily combination skin and mild rosacea ended with a compromised barrier, while an oily-skinned reviewer found it among the gentlest retinols they had used. James Just Now found it stronger than Paula's Choice CLINICAL 1% Retinol Treatment, with more results but heavy ongoing peeling.

highlights.text: peeling, dryness and redness are common

paras: Reviewers who liked it describe a watery gel that sinks in fast, leaves a natural glow without shine and works as a layer under any moisturizer, including on dry, sensitive and dry combination skin with no breakouts. Others were less taken: one with very dry skin saw only a small long-term gain and found two pumps too little, and a clinician judged the formula thin, with key ingredients low in the list. Several note it is a splurge, and some say a cheaper hyaluronic or Korean serum could do a similar job.

Reviewers who liked it call it a nice midweight, whipped cream with no fragrance and little irritation that works for normal, combination and dry skin, including under makeup. Takes split on value and hydration: several rated hydration as basic, or not moisturizing enough, and many called it pricey next to a drugstore ceramide moisturizer. Skin type matters most: oily or acne-prone reviewers reported greasiness and breakouts and pointed to Isopropyl Isostearate, while a dry-skinned reviewer found no dew and some stinging. Geeky Posh points to CeraVe Moisturizing Cream as a plainer option with ceramides, cholesterol, hyaluronic acid and petrolatum.

Reviewers who liked it describe a clear gel with real AHA and BHA activity that blends in, leaves no residue and gradually improves texture and tone when used two to three nights a week, in a well-designed airtight pump. Takes split on skin type: oily and combination skin did well, while dry and very dry skin saw dryness, peeling and little change, and several complained about the price. Stephanie Nicole prefers Sunday Riley Good Genes Lactic Acid Treatment, which they can use every night, and says it blows this serum out of the water for their very dry skin. Roxanne Latulippe finds it gentler than The Ordinary Glycolic Acid 7% Exfoliating Toner, which they find irritating and stripping.

highlights.text: blows this serum out of the water

paras: Reviewers who liked it describe a light, non-greasy lotion that goes on clear, absorbs well and sits under makeup, with the best reports coming from redness-prone, combination and acne-prone skin. Takes split on comfort and finish: some saw a white cast right away or after reapplying, others felt burning, tingling or peeling, and one found it shiny over dehydrated-looking skin. Dr. Daniel Sugai compares it with a mineral matte sunscreen that blended well but lacked niacinamide and antioxidants, and still calls this one a go-to for acne or rosacea-prone skin.

highlights.text: go-to for acne or rosacea-prone skin

paras: Reviewers liked the natural matte finish and light tint, which blends into fair to medium skin and works well under foundation. Takes split on skin tone and layering: one reviewer said it made them look paler, another saw a bad white cast on dark, oily skin, and a third saw peeling when a third layer went on. Josh recommends a different EltaMD mineral sunscreen for anyone with a darker skin tone, since this one looks too light. Melanoma Mom compares it with a cheaper tinted sunscreen from another brand that feels the same but looks more orange and is water resistant for longer.

highlights.text: peeling when a third layer went on

paras: Reviewers praise the hydration, a natural finish with a soft glow and a light or absent scent, mainly for dry, mature or dehydrated skin. Takes split on texture and cast: one found it melts in after priming the pump, while others found it thick and pasty, or saw a white cast on most people above a fair complexion. The Budget Dermatologist compares it with EltaMD UV Clear Broad-Spectrum SPF 46, which they send acne-prone and rosacea-prone skin to instead. Sally Choi, MD calls it effective but not worth the price and picks a different EltaMD mineral sunscreen to buy instead.

Reviewers agree it is a chemical lotion with no white cast that goes on easily and works under foundation or BB cream. Takes split on oil control and skin type: one found a heavy, slick feel and breakouts on oily, acne-prone, sensitive skin, while another with combination skin leaning oily found it dried fast without grease but accentuated dry patches. Dr Dray prefers another Eucerin SPF 50 face lotion for looks and easier spreading, but picks this one for anyone who does not get along with hyaluronic acid.

highlights.text: works under foundation or BB cream

paras: Reviewers praise a creamy, fragrance-free cleanser that is gentle on sensitive and irritated skin, foams lightly and leaves skin soft rather than tight. Takes split on dryness and makeup removal: one reviewer found skin very dry afterwards and will not repurchase, another found it stung the eyes, and some said makeup needs patient massage, extra passes or a second cleanse. BeatleBabe compares it with a red clay mask cleanser from the same brand, which was only okay, and says this one made them a believer in the brand.

highlights.text: gentle on sensitive and irritated skin

paras: Reviewers praise long-lasting hydration without a greasy feel, a soothing oatmeal and ceramide formula, and its use on dry, sensitive and irritated skin, with some also using it on the body and hands. Takes split on weight: it is described as spreadable and lotion-like by one reviewer and as thick as a winter coat by another, and some expect it to feel too heavy in summer. Dr. Arsalan Aspires compares it with Kiehl's Ultra Facial Cream, prefers this one for sensitive or irritation-prone skin, and finds the Kiehl's cream heavier with more chance of oiliness.

Reviewers liked a creamy, gentle lather that cleans without leaving skin tight or dry, and place it with sensitive, redness-prone and combination skin. Takes split slightly on hydration: one calls it hydrating and barrier-supporting, while another says it does not leave skin hydrated, only comfortable, and uses it as the second cleanse. One reviewer also notes it contains fragrance, which matters for anyone sensitive to it.

Reviewers praise an easy pump, a gel cream that melts in and hydrates, a light fruity scent, and brighter, less puffy under eyes. They differ on how fast results show: one liked an instant tint that corrects dark circles but saw only subtle long-term change after about a week and a half, while another says it handles puffiness, dark circles and fine lines. Beauty Within compares it with a thicker, richer retinol eye cream from the same brand and suggests this one in the morning and that one at night. Kimberly Gamble calls it a tie for favorite with a banana eye cream from another brand.

Reviewers praise instant hydration, a light, bouncy gel texture and a dewy finish that wears well under makeup, mostly on normal and combination skin. Takes split on skin type and season: one found it too dewy by day and greasy overnight on oily skin, another got repeat breakouts on combination skin, and a winter reviewer found the juicy feel faded and wanted something thicker. Nadia Vega compares it with a richer polypeptide cream from another brand that moisturizes more, and with a more watery moisturizer that suits very sensitive skin better. Kimberly Gamble compares it with Kiehl's Ultra Facial Cream, a traditional cream they prefer at night for the dry parts of the face.

Reviewers praise a lightweight gel that absorbs fast, hydrates and rarely stings, with smoother texture, fewer breakouts and less redness building up over weeks, mostly on acne-prone, combination and sensitive skin. Takes split on strength: some call it a gentle starter acid with slow, modest results, one found it underwhelming next to other BHA products, one saw about a week of purging, and another mild peeling when layering products. Cassandra Bankson compares it with The Ordinary AHA 30% + BHA 2% Peeling Solution, finding it nothing like that peel with only 1% AHA, and suggests the peel once a week with this serum on the off days. Beauty Detective says its results cannot beat a salicylic acid exfoliant from another brand, so it stays pleasant rather than a game-changer.

Reviewers with sensitive, rosacea-prone or dehydrated skin describe a gentle overnight gel that leaves skin smoother, softer and plumper by morning. Takes split on strength: one reviewer with textured skin found it potent enough to sting during the first uses, while experienced acid users may find it too gentle. Nadia Vega likes the hydration but prefers an overnight niacinamide mask for smaller looking pores.

Reviewers mostly like it as a quick, cooling hydration step with a watermelon scent, used at night or as a morning prep before makeup. Takes split on handling: the thin sheet tears easily, slips down the face and can leave tacky serum or bits of jelly behind. 𝓚𝓾𝓲𝓻𝓪 𝓙𝓱𝓪𝓷𝓪𝓲ꨄ︎ finds the slightly sticky afterfeel similar to Glow Recipe Watermelon Glow Niacinamide Dew Drops.

highlights.text: tears easily, slips down the face

paras: Reviewers like the dewy glow and the way it helps foundation go on smoothly, and several use it as a primer or highlighter as much as a serum. Takes split on feel: some found it sticky or tacky, while others said it dries down fast without any stickiness. Julianna Henricus prefers The Ordinary Niacinamide 10% + Zinc 1% and will not repurchase, and Cassandra Bankson ranked it second from the bottom in a lineup of niacinamide products as a treatment.

Reviewers who loved it praise a hydrating, slightly syrupy toner that does not sting or dry skin out, with some adding that it suits dry, normal or acne-prone skin. Takes split on results: it exfoliates lightly, pores did not visibly tighten, and a dermatologist reviewer objected to the pore-tight name. Live That Glow points to The INKEY List PHA Toner as a cheaper option with similar results according to some users, while Nadia Vega finds it gentler than a stronger PHA exfoliating liquid and more hydrating than another exfoliating toner.

Reviewers like the very fine, even spray and the fresh watermelon scent, using it between skincare steps, under makeup or as a midday refresher. Takes split on benefit: some felt refreshed and plumped with a dewy finish that lasted hours, while others felt it added little real hydration, did not set makeup and was not unique. beautybyjessicalee picked it over a cheaper grocery-store watermelon mist, which sprayed harsher and stung slightly.

Reviewers who like it describe a thick, very hydrating toner that leaves skin soft, plump and supple, with a lavender scent that some enjoy. Takes split on feel and tolerance: some found it tacky or sticky once layered past two or three coats, and one reviewer blamed the lavender fragrance for irritation and itching. Kaori's Skincare Journal prefers a pure hyaluronic acid lotion that absorbs better and is far more hypoallergenic.

Reviewers praise a lightweight cream-gel that blends in quickly, leaves no white cast or scent and sits well under makeup, with several calling it a favorite among Korean chemical sunscreens. Takes split on finish and skin type: it dries from dewy to a velvety or satin finish, but oily or combination skin found it shiny or not very mattifying, and one reviewer with sensitive skin saw spots, bumps and redness. Lab Muffin Beauty Science calls it slightly more moisturizing and creamy than Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun: Rice + Probiotics SPF 50+, and clarity kat picked it as the overall winner over Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun Aqua-Fresh: Rice + B5 SPF 50+. My Skincare Regime lists SKIN1004 Hyalu-Cica Water-Fit Sun Serum as a dupe.

Reviewers with dry skin praise a cushiony, non-greasy cream that absorbs quickly, leaves skin soft and holds up under sunscreen and foundation. Takes split on skin type: it is described as best for dry skin, one reviewer with oily combination skin did not feel overly hydrated, and another flagged soybean oil and myristic acid as pore clogging and called it basic and expensive for what it is. Katie Hoke already loves an SPF 30 moisturizer and wishes this one had SPF.

highlights.text: basic and expensive for what it is

paras: Reviewers who loved it describe a lightweight, hydrating lotion that sits well under makeup with a healthy glow and no white cast. Takes split on finish: some found it shiny and needed powder or blotting through the day, others found it almost invisible, and one disliked the smell. Kate Tsirkunov found it the gentler choice next to Supergoop! Unseen Sunscreen SPF 50, which once made them cry within fifteen minutes. alex greyson calls it very similar to the original version of this sunscreen, only a little more lightweight and hydrating.

Reviewers who loved it describe a creamy, nourishing serum that calmed redness and irritation and helped a compromised barrier. Takes split on texture and use: one reviewer found it weirdly dry and not hydrating and would only reach for it when the barrier is compromised, while others layer it under a moisturizer. Kelly Driscoll finds it a bit more moisturizing and slightly thicker than another barrier repair serum in the same roundup, and Nadia Vega liked it and a cica ampoule for different reasons.

Reviewers with combination, acne-prone, normal to dry and sensitive skin all found it a gentle way into glycolic acid, leaving skin smoother and softer with only a mild sting or tingle. Takes differ on strength and results: one reviewer calls it a solid step up from 2 percent exfoliants but says people used to 8 or 10 percent products may find it does less, and prefers it to a toner that left their skin dry and tight. Another found it left skin very oily the next morning on dehydrated days, while a third saw smoother texture and smaller-looking pores, though not gone.

highlights.text: a gentle way into glycolic acid

paras: Reviewers praise the hydrating, jelly-like gel, which left rosacea, combination and dry skin clean and soft without dryness or tightness. Takes split on cleaning power and lather: one reviewer found it makes little lather and doubts it would take off makeup or sunscreen without rubbing, while another found it lathers nicely and removes daily makeup and sunscreen. Comparing it with the old formula, alex greyson finds the reformulated gel silkier and more hydrating, though it can feel a little too hydrating at times.

Reviewers like how light it feels on the face and body: it absorbs fast, leaves no white cast and gives a natural glow rather than a sticky feel. Skin types vary, from oily and combination to dry or winter skin, and one reviewer says it holds up on sweaty, humid days. Abbey Yung finds it thicker and creamier than a cooling lotion from the same brand but lighter than a heavier SPF 70 daily lotion, while Dr Dray finds it less moisturizing than a richer sunscreen made for dry skin and better for sweaty conditions. The downsides are mild: the alcohol can be a little drying, one reviewer noticed a scent despite the fragrance free label, one had hard, chunky bits that would not rub in, and value is only okay for some.

highlights.text: absorbs fast, leaves no white cast
alcohol can be a little drying

paras: Reviewers with dry, sensitive, retinoid-irritated or barrier-damaged skin praise how it soothed stinging, redness and tightness, mostly as a thick night layer. Takes split on texture and skin type: it leaves a dewy sheen, can look white until rubbed in, and was too rich for daily use on oily or blockage-prone skin, where one reviewer got new blocked pores. MissLJBeauty finds it lighter and quicker to absorb than CeraVe Healing Ointment, but still too thick to wear under makeup.

highlights.text: too thick to wear under makeup

paras: Reviewers with oily, combination and sensitive skin like how well the gel foams and clears oil without irritation, with some seeing calmer breakouts. Takes split on dryness: one reviewer found twice-daily use left skin tight and a little stripped and cut back to once a day, others noticed only slight dryness on snowy mornings or around the cheeks, and reviewers warn dry or normal skin should skip it. BERyNICE prefers La Roche-Posay Toleriane Purifying Foaming Facial Wash for acne-prone, sensitive skin, partly for its niacinamide, and says this one can suit skin that is only oily.

Reviewers with sensitive skin who used it as a first retinol say it stayed gentle, with brighter, more even skin after a few weeks to a few months of regular use. Takes split sharply on the formula: some reviewers dislike the fragrance, denatured alcohol and dropper bottle, and one finds the cream and serum hybrid texture a miss. Dr. Ashwini Megur suggests newcomers start with a lower strength retinol serum instead, and calls this one poor value next to far cheaper retinoids.

highlights.text: fragrance, denatured alcohol and dropper bottle

paras: Reviewers with sensitive, dry, normal and combination skin praise the light, quick-absorbing texture, the near absence of scent and the gentle hydration. Takes split by skin type and layering: one reviewer with oily, acne-prone skin got cystic breakouts, one with very dry skin used it for years but moved to a lighter cream once skin recovered, and others found it pilled under sunscreen or makeup or left a dull, dry finish. Only_Jenny finds it lighter than a thicker SPF moisturizer tried on the other half of their face, and ReadHead by Roux Atelier recommends CeraVe PM Facial Moisturizing Lotion instead.

Reviewers like the soft, lotion-like texture, the lack of fragrance and the hydrated, smooth feel, including on skin dried out by tretinoin and on sensitive skin. Takes split on oily skin and cleaning power: one reviewer with oily skin liked it while on tretinoin, others felt it cleans less and may not suit oily skin, and one saw redness and bumps within a week. Dr. Ashwini Megur rates it above CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser, Enjoy the View Blog finds it creamier and softer than that cleanser, and benenon picks Vanicream Gentle Facial Cleanser as the overall favorite but finds this one better for drier winter months.

Reviewers like the soft, quick lather that cleans without a squeaky or tight feeling and without irritation, on normal, oily, combination and acne-prone skin. Dry skin is where takes split: Beautyistic finds it non-drying but not hydrating, while ganniyat ao finds it much more moisturizing than CeraVe Foaming Facial Cleanser, and reviewers say dry skin may get drier in colder months or needs the hydrating version. Beautyistic also finds it a touch more refined than CeraVe Foaming Facial Cleanser or Neutrogena Ultra Gentle Daily Cleanser, and says the CeraVe one may be slightly more hydrating while this one rinses cleaner. Dr. Arsalan Aspires points dry skin to La Roche-Posay Toleriane Hydrating Gentle Facial Cleanser instead.

Reviewers like the watery, layerable milky texture, the dewy glow and the hydration, with no fragrance and no clogged pores or acne, and many suit it to dry or dehydrated skin. Takes split on richness and season: it felt too heavy or greasy for oily skin in summer and not nourishing enough alone in winter for others, and one reviewer found it did not brighten. The reformulated version divides opinions too: JQ LEEJQ finds the Cerapeptide version very similar to the original and a little longer wearing, while Kelly Driscoll finds the new formula lighter, less rich and a disappointing replacement for dry winter skin.

highlights.text: too heavy or greasy for oily skin

paras: Reviewers who loved it describe a cooling, jelly-like layer that dries without a tacky feel and leaves skin plump and soft by morning. Takes split on fragrance and acne: one reviewer with very sensitive skin blamed the scent for breakouts, and another woke up dry and with cysts on oily, acne-prone skin. Keeping Up With The Queen finds a thicker collagen cream better for very dry skin, and this mask better for a refreshing, spa-like feel.

highlights.text: leaves skin plump and soft by morning

paras: Reviewers who loved it dab it on pimples at night and find them smaller, flatter or less red within a day or two, though several say it needs time rather than working overnight. Deep cystic spots are where takes split: some found cystic acne cleared more slowly or not at all, and one reviewer saw no change on a cluster of pimples. Jenz BeautyStyle found a mud-colored, mint-smelling drying lotion from another brand helped a spot as well, with a shorter shelf life once opened.

highlights.text: cleared more slowly or not at all

paras: Reviewers who loved it spray it as a midday refresher, a makeup setting spray or a first layer after washing, with several noting no breakouts even on sensitive or oily skin. Takes split on feel and fragrance: some found the scent loud and the finish sticky, while others found it faint and dried down nicely. Maati Sll finds it works as well as a popular makeup setting mist for refreshing skin and setting makeup, though the setting time may differ.

highlights.text: spray it as a midday refresher
found the scent loud and the finish sticky

paras: Reviewers who loved it describe a creamy green clay mask with a fresh, clean scent that leaves skin soft, smooth and slightly lifted after 15 to 20 minutes. Results are where takes split: some saw no visible change beyond softer skin or slight brightness, while one reported a glow from the first use. Most also noted it did not burn, dry out or break out dry and sensitive skin.

highlights.text: no visible change beyond softer skin

paras: Reviewers who liked it praise a water-like essence that sinks in within seconds, has no scent and layers easily under the next step, with hydrated, brighter skin after a couple of weeks. Takes split on the fifth formula: one reviewer found it did nothing and was not hydrating enough even as a toner, and another calls it watered down compared with older versions. Kelly Driscoll finds a richer enriched version of the same essence plumper, and this lighter one better for watery rehydration.

highlights.text: watered down compared with older versions

paras: Reviewers praise a creamy but light cream that hydrates without a greasy finish, leaves skin supple by morning and has little to no smell. Takes split on the essential oils: some flagged bergamot and lavender oils as possible irritants and advised a patch test, especially for sensitive skin. Hallie Bradley finds this cream, rather than the viral mixsoon Bean Essence, the one that suited their dry skin.

highlights.text: bergamot and lavender oils as possible irritants

paras: Reviewers who loved it describe a stretchy, non-sticky essence that leaves skin plump, glowy and smoother, often with no irritation on oily, combination or sensitive skin. Takes split on exfoliation and hydration: some massage it in to lift dead skin and blackheads, while others saw little come off or say it is not a true exfoliant. Nipun Kapur finds COSRX Advanced Snail 96 Mucin Power Essence more hydrating but this essence better for brightness and pores, while Dr Dray sees less glow and elasticity than from that one. One reviewer with acne-prone skin got breakouts that worsened and stopped using it.

Reviewers who loved it describe a watery, quick-drying liquid that exfoliates without burning, stinging or peeling, with fewer breakouts, smoother texture and less congestion over a few weeks. Skin Carma NYC calls it as effective an exfoliating toner as Paula's Choice SKIN PERFECTING 2% BHA Liquid Exfoliant, though less pleasant to use, while Kisha A. Goody prefers this one for being gentler and more hydrating. Kasandra Williams found it did not clear their cystic acne the way Paula's Choice SKIN PERFECTING 2% BHA Liquid Exfoliant did, and Dr Dray flags its citrus extracts.

highlights.text: exfoliates without burning, stinging or peeling
did not clear their cystic acne

paras: Reviewers who loved it describe a creamy SPF 50 chemical-filter moisturizer that rubs in invisibly with no white cast, leaves a dewy glow and works as both moisturizer and makeup base. Takes split on skin type: reviewers with oily or acne-prone skin found the dew turns greasy in warm weather or caused pimples, and several reserve it for fall and winter. The Daley Dose and SkinCare Stacy both prefer Naturium UV Reflect Antioxidant SPF 50, which is thinner and serum-like, for acne-prone skin and summer, while Jetvinchy picks a less dewy mineral SPF 30 for oily skin.

Reviewers who loved it describe a thin-spreading, scentless 10% glycolic gel in a pump bottle that exfoliates without burning, itching or drying when used once or twice a week. They also warn it is easy to overuse and that too much feels tacky, with one reviewer whose skin reacts badly to most acids keeping it off the face and using it on hands and feet. On the Harp uses it as a replacement for a favorite liquid glycolic acid and prefers the gel form as more effective than a liquid.

highlights.text: exfoliates without burning, itching or drying

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it as a gentle exfoliant for sensitive skin and for anyone new to acids, with a light, quick-absorbing texture. One reviewer found it too gentle to use every other day, and another marked it down because the citrus extracts could irritate, based on the ingredient list. Marie Antoinette moved to it after finding The Ordinary Lactic Acid 10% + HA too strong at times, and says it does not sting like many other acids.

highlights.text: too gentle to use every other day

paras: Reviewers praise the silky, moisturizing texture, which sits well under concealer and makeup and stays gentle around the eyes. Takes split on results: one reviewer saw a soft-focus blur of fine lines, while another saw no effect beyond moisture despite the peptide promise. Reviewers also said it does not help dark circles, and one called a retinol based eye cream the better route for fine lines.

Reviewers praise a creamy, quick-absorbing texture, and some reported no irritation or sensitivity at 0.10%. Takes split on hydration and results: one reviewer found it not hydrating enough alone and always follows with a moisturizer, while another noticed a hydrated glow. One reviewer who had tried the lower 0.05% strength found the results similar and calls the 0.10% better suited to wrinkles, while another advises beginners to start on the 0.05%.

Reviewers like the light gel texture that absorbs fast without a greasy or sticky feel, and the hydration it gives dry under-eyes. They also report no irritation, including on eyes that react to allergies or to other products in the line. No reviewer raised a complaint, and the details that vary are how they use it, such as keeping the tube in the refrigerator or wearing it under concealer.

highlights.text: light gel texture that absorbs fast

paras: Reviewers praise the light, jelly-like texture that hydrates dry skin and absorbs fast without feeling greasy, including on an eczema flare. Takes split on tolerance: one found it gentle and expected it to suit rosacea or eczema, while another noted many comments about pimples and stinging and found it films on the face when used alone. That reviewer prefers it for spot hydration on fine lines, covered with a heavier moisturizer.

highlights.text: hydrates dry skin and absorbs fast
films on the face when used alone

paras: Reviewers with oily and combination skin praise the cool, watery gel that absorbs quickly, leaves no shine and sits well under makeup. Takes split on dry skin: one found hydration faded within hours on oily but dehydrated skin, and another needed a richer cream on very dry areas, while a third called it suitable for dry skin as well as oily. The strongest complaint came from a reviewer with sensitive, acne-prone skin who got burning, irritation and tiny breakouts, and fragrance and silicones also put off other reviewers.

highlights.text: cool, watery gel that absorbs quickly

paras: The reviewers who liked it have oily or acne-prone skin and use it carefully, such as diluted with water, once a day, or with a moisturizer afterwards, with one reporting cleared clogged pores and faded marks over time. Takes split sharply on skin type, since reviewers with sensitive, eczema-prone, normal or non-acne-prone skin reported dry, rough, itchy or red skin within days. Hyram did not use it but criticised the stripping cleansing agent, preservative, fragrance and dyes, and suggested KraveBeauty Matcha Hemp Hydrating Cleanser for dry acne-prone skin.

highlights.text: cleared clogged pores and faded marks
dry, rough, itchy or red skin

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the hydrating, glowing finish of this thick, fermented essence toner, which suits dull, dehydrated or dry skin best. Takes split on the scent, which some enjoy while others, including one reviewer with sensitive skin, found it itchy or irritating, and on combination or oily skin, where it can feel too rich or tacky and cause tiny bumps in humid weather. Several reviewers also said it layers well in small amounts but turns sticky when stacked too many times.

Reviewers praise the lightweight, fast-absorbing texture that layers well and stays gentle, including on sensitive and reactive skin. Takes split on results: some saw dark spots and fresh post-acne marks fade over time, while one reviewer with melasma and freckles saw little change and warned against expecting quick whitening. Boundlesswithshalu prefers it to Anua Niacinamide 10% + TXA 4% Serum for sensitive or combination skin, since the Anua serum works faster but feels harsher.

Reviewers praise the balanced, hydrating cream and its brightening, depuffing and glowing finish, and find the new tube packaging easier to use than the old syringe. Takes differ on strength and use: one reviewer with sensitive skin uses it about every other night, while another advises easing in and using it in the evening only. Dark circles are the main limit, with one reviewer seeing bluish or reddish circles brighten after a few weeks and another suggesting a caffeine serum first for very dark purplish circles.

Reviewers mostly like it for acne-prone and combination skin, praising a light cream-gel texture that spreads easily and results on redness, post-acne marks and bumpy texture. Takes split on strength: some call it too mild for breakouts, pigmentation or severe acne, while others saw clear gains within weeks. Dr. Arsalan Aspires prefers it over The Ordinary Azelaic Acid Suspension 10% for acne and post-acne marks, and picks the Ordinary one for rosacea-type redness or a tight budget.

highlights.text: light cream-gel texture that spreads easily

paras: Reviewers like it as a gentle, hydrating vitamin C eye cream that absorbs fast and layers well under concealer or sunscreen. Results are described as brightening more than correcting, easing shadows and dullness without fully fixing genetic dark circles. Sensitive skin that dislikes pure vitamin C coped well for one reviewer, while another got stinging when dabbing too close to the eyelids.

highlights.text: gentle, hydrating vitamin C eye cream
without fully fixing genetic dark circles

paras: Reviewers mostly use it as a gentler way into retinol, praising a soft, creamy texture and the pump packaging, with sensitive and rosacea-prone skin managing it a few nights a week. Results are described as smoother texture, softer fine lines and a brighter look rather than a dramatic change. Mad About Skin finds it much gentler and less irritating than Paula's Choice CLINICAL 1% Retinol Treatment, which they loved but found drying. The one mixed reviewer liked it as a soothing partner to tretinoin but was unsure about repurchasing.

Reviewers agree it is a strong retinol that needs a slow start, usually once a week or every other night, with a moisturizer on top. Takes split on tolerance: one reviewer got very little sensitivity from a gradual build up and another repurchases it as a favorite, while a third got irritation and painful pimples however rarely they used it. Results are described as softer, glowier skin, with no clear change in fine lines or acne scars after 30 days for one reviewer.

Reviewers like it for smoother, softer skin and lasting hydration, mostly on combination, dry and older skin, with no reactions for most. Weight is where takes differ: it is called watery by some and quite rich by others, and one reviewer with sensitive skin saw more redness along the T-zone. alex greyson says it hydrates longer than Paula's Choice SKIN BALANCING Pore-Reducing Toner, but would gravitate to Byoma Milky Toner for repurchasing since it worked a little better for them.

highlights.text: smoother, softer skin and lasting hydration
saw more redness along the T-zone

paras: Reviewers mostly like it for a watery, lightweight feel, fast absorption and a natural or satin finish that sits well under makeup, on oily, combination and normal skin. Takes split on hydration and finish: some find it moisturizing enough to replace a moisturizer, while others want one underneath, find it pills if rubbed in too much, or see skin looking oily by afternoon. Eye stinging and breakouts were the main complaints from those who did not get on with it, including reviewers with sensitive skin. alex greyson names Naturium Dew-Glow Moisturizer SPF 50 as a beautiful alternative with a similar moisturizer texture, and would not replace a favorite sunscreen with this one.

highlights.text: pills if rubbed in too much

paras: Reviewers like it as a lightweight, non-irritating toner for normal, combination and oily skin, with a fresh feel that layers well under serums, sunscreen and a liquid exfoliant. Hydration is light, so reviewers point dry skin elsewhere, and the benefits for pores and breakouts are described as subtle, though one reviewer noticed pores looking more visible after stopping for a few weeks. Nadia Vega says Glow Recipe Watermelon Glow PHA+BHA Pore-Tight Toner feels more hydrating and suits newer skincare users wanting hydration, but calls this one the better value.

Reviewers praise it for clearing pores, whiteheads and spots on oily, combination and acne-prone skin, often within a week or two of regular use. Tolerance depends on how often it is used: one reviewer got tight, tingly skin from twice daily use in winter, another cut back to two evenings a week, and a third found it gentle yet fast-acting. A blog finds COSRX BHA Blackhead Power Liquid milder and better for keeping skin clear, while this gel did more for congested skin.

Reviewers praise it as a gentle, water-like exfoliant that absorbs quickly, did not sting even on sensitive or irritated skin, and left skin smoother and glowier. Results split on strength: several saw clearer skin, faded dark spots or fewer breakouts, while the mixed pair found it preventative only for hormonal acne or could not see a change in acne or pigmentation. Several advise starting two or three times a week rather than the twice daily on the label, and keeping it apart from retinol. cathy on skincare finds the finish oilier looking than The Ordinary Salicylic Acid 2% Solution.

Reviewers mostly like it for smoother, more even skin and a glow, often used two or three nights a week, as a thin gel that absorbs quickly with a moisturizer on top. Takes split on gentleness: it stung briefly or dried the face for some, was too gentle for stubborn pigmentation or acne scars for another, and is seen as better suited to drier skin than oily. Beautiful With Brains finds the lotion version of this 8% AHA very similar but better for dry skin, with the gel better for normal or combination skin.

Reviewers praise it as a light, hydrating and calming toner that suits dry to very dry skin and helps skin irritated by retinol or exfoliants feel better. Takes split mostly on skin type: One reviewer warns that several of its oils are fungal acne triggers, so an alcohol-free centella toner suits acne-prone skin far better, though they still pick this one overall for its more instant results. Others used it for an extra moisture boost after a dry winter, and one with mild to moderate rosacea found it slightly calming without feeling greasy.

Reviewers like it as a light gel serum that absorbs quickly, hydrates and leaves a dewy sheen without feeling greasy. One finds it gentle for dry, sensitive skin and easy to layer with serums containing actives, while another saw less red skintone and post-acne marks almost completely faded over several weeks. Results were more modest for one reviewer, whose skin looked healthier but was probably still not glassy enough to go viral.

highlights.text: light gel serum that absorbs quickly
still not glassy enough to go viral

paras: Reviewers like the three sizes, the barely visible clear patches and the overnight wear, with most seeing a pimple look smaller or less red by morning. Several find them hard to peel off the sheet. Opinions split on grip and power: one found the thicker patch stays put without lifting, while another saw bubbles and patchy sticking, and one woke up without a patch several times. A reviewer after big irritated cysts found nothing was drawn out, and others say the patches only make pimples less noticeable, not gone.

highlights.text: smaller or less red by morning
hard to peel off the sheet
woke up without a patch several times

paras: Reviewers praise a watery, quick-absorbing toner with a gentle PHA exfoliant that hydrates without a heavy or sticky feel, and many used it on oily or acne-prone skin. Takes split on strength: one finds it too mild for very acne-prone skin or open pores, one found it plain and a little tacky as a normal toner, and a cosmetic formulator warns that even a mild daily exfoliant can be too much for skin of color. alex greyson finds it even more watery than the SKIN1004 Madagascar Centella Ampoule, which feels closer to a face oil, and adds that anyone sensitive to niacinamide may prefer the ampoule.

highlights.text: too mild for very acne-prone skin
too much for skin of color

paras: Reviewers praise a very lightweight, serum-like sunscreen with a dewy, hydrated glow, no white cast and no pilling under makeup. Takes split on finish and skin type: very oily skin may find it too dewy, very dry or dehydrated skin may want something richer, and several note it is not sweat or water resistant. Diba's Quest contrasts it with the SKIN1004 Centella Air-Fit Suncream Plus, a soft-tinted mineral cream that left a white cast on darker areas, while this serum left none.

Reviewers praise a watery, toner-like ampoule that absorbs in seconds without stickiness and gradually calms redness and irritation, with several using it on sensitive or retinoid-irritated skin. Takes split on strength: the mixed reviewers call hydration moderate and the effect too mild for severe flare-ups or a fast fix, and most reviewers say very dry skin needs a richer cream on top.
